scope: Reviewed high-risk naming, collaborative lore proposals, and contested combat actions in auditorium incursion.

decisions.reason: At L1159, player William Webb explicitly designated the Spiritual Weapon as an encyclopedia ('Obviously, it's an encyclopedia britannica'). Per explicit authorial directive, all nun ruler / straightedge jokes (L1164) are excised as OOC banter into the skipped ledger. Dravin's weapon is unified canonically as the scholarly tome/encyclopedia across Scenes 7, 8, and 9, preserving absolute prop continuity into the Scene 9 climax where Dravin physically slams his book down to knock out the Gorgon.

Pierre's outward banter and vanity ('Pierre is a lover, not a fighter') is grounded in deep-POV prose as a charismatic coping mechanism masking near-panic from previous monster encounters, preserving comedic timing while raising psychological stakes without inventing ungrounded bloodline lore.

decisions.contributor: William Webb, Sophie Foreman Noone, Luke Foreman
decisions.reason: Dravin does not know he is casting magic (per DEC-026); his unconscious protective intent projects glowing threshold runes ('SPARE') from his coat signet. Alfie, who perceives the living typography of magic, intervenes to pluck and twist the letter into 'SPORE' to harm only the hostiles, maintaining Dravin's scholar archetype while honoring the campaign's linguistic spellcraft physics.
The GM wraps up at the edge of the Lost Roads; no further PC actions played in this session.

critiques.speaker: Alfie
critiques.quote: Dr. Aris Thorne stumbled against the mahogany edge of the podium, her knuckles turning bone-white against the railing as she surveyed the ruins of her lecture hall. Overhead, the emergency sprinklers sputtered their final droplets into the murky puddles below. She stared in unvarnished terror at the shattered rows of seats, the scorched upholstery, and the bound, gray-skinned woman lying motionless upon the carpet. Alfie hopped onto the brass trim of the stage apron, folding his small carved arms across his tiny linen trench coat. His painted seashell button eyes narrowed to sharp slits. "I do not love when people call me a doll. Let's just start there."
critiques.comment: How is this possible that we didn't have this checked by the pipeline or no? The agents picked this up as a reader to flow with. Alfie is responding to dialogue that isn't even said by the professor in this version
critiques.resolution_notes: Resolved in `s6-scene-10-alt.md` (L1444). Restored Dr. Thorne's spoken dialogue where she stammers in shock and asks if Alfie is a talking doll, providing direct conversational context for Alfie's indignant response.

critiques.speaker: Prof. Edward Dravin
critiques.quote: Professor Dravin wiped the heavy condensation from his wire-rimmed spectacles, tucking his leather-bound lexicon securely beneath his arm. "I will alternate between *Spare the Dying* and *Spore the Dying* to keep her unconscious and alive," Dravin observed calmly, ensuring the creature's volatile pulse remained subdued.

critiques.resolution_notes: Resolved in `s6-scene-10-alt.md` (L1460). Kept Dravin's dialogue in authentic character: 'I do not entirely understand how this resonance works, but I gather I can keep her alive, or cause deadly fungal spores to sprout from her flesh.'

critiques.speaker: Pierre
critiques.quote: Pierre adjusted his woolen beret with an imperious, mock-sympathetic flourish, looking down his nose at the trembling academic. "You are very important to your own story, Madame. I listened to your entire lecture, and nothing of merit was spoken outside the vision. Take all of your money, invest everything into this solitary research, sever all ties with your colleagues, and flee into the dark. We have a janitor's cart to commandeer." Overcome with panic, Thorne bolted across the green room and shoved through the emergency exit into the rainy night.
critiques.comment: I don't mind the truncation here, but I think there's some back and forth that's worth doing where she's trying to understand what's happening and in revenge for calling her a doll. The team collectively convinces her that she was the reason all this happened and that she's very important and that she needs to go be a manic conspiracy theorist basically which is the best revenge they can think of for calling Alfie a doll
critiques.resolution_notes: Resolved in `s6-scene-10-alt.md` (L1500). Staged the team convincing Dr. Thorne that she is the central figure in a vast occult conspiracy as playful revenge for calling Alfie a doll, driving Thorne into manic fringe research as she flees.

critiques.speaker: Alfie
critiques.quote: "This is incredible," Alfie whispered in genuine awe, perching atop a balsa skyscraper to admire the tiny balconies before hopping down to help push the rolling bin toward the door. "All right, back to the lost roads with our hostage."
